provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Clean family batch, book archetype. Small per-visit tickets that only pay off as recurring plans, so products stay cheap and schedule-shaped. Fresh Fern fails CTA contrast. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: A room-by-room checklist for a standard clean, a deep clean and a move-out clean: baseboards, inside the oven, inside the fridge, ceiling fans, interior windows, and which ones are add-ons
pageStructurePlus.why: People compare house cleaners by what gets cleaned, not by adjectives. A checklist settles the 'does that include the oven' question before they book.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Empty-home pricing by bedroom count, the landlord walkthrough checklist, appliance interiors, cabinet wipe-outs, and how keys or lockbox codes are handed over
pageStructurePlus.why: Tenants and sellers buy a move-out clean on a deadline. They want a fixed price and a date, and they book whoever shows both first.

pageStructurePlus.section: Your first clean and home access
pageStructurePlus.contains: Why the first visit runs longer, how to prep, pets at home, entry codes and lockboxes, supplies the team brings, fragrance-free options, and whether the same cleaner comes back
pageStructurePlus.why: The first booking is the nervous one. Answering access, pets and supplies ahead of time removes the reasons people stall at the Book button.

pageStructurePlus.contains: How to report a missed spot within a day, a short form that takes a note and a picture, and the free re-clean of that area at the next opening
pageStructurePlus.why: Clients drop a house cleaner over one missed bathroom that nobody fixed. A written re-clean promise answers that fear before the first visit.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Turnover cleaning between guests, linen changes, restocking, a checklist the host can see, same-day turnaround windows and per-turnover pricing by bedroom
pageStructurePlus.why: Hosts book cleaning by checkout time and need the turnover done before the next check-in. A separate page wins a buyer the family page doesn't speak to.

designDirections.name: Price in Two Taps
designDirections.bestFor: Solo cleaners and small teams who need the bed-and-bath price on screen before anyone calls
designDirections.headlineSample: House cleaning in {City}, priced before you book
designDirections.whyItFits: Peach Sorbet's soft rounded type reads like a friendly neighbour, and the coral button sits easily next to a price table.

designDirections.name: Book the Recurring Clean
designDirections.bestFor: Teams of a few cleaners selling weekly and biweekly plans with real open slots
designDirections.headlineSample: Weekly and biweekly house cleaning in {City}, booked online
designDirections.whyItFits: The family combo, Fresh Fern, fails CTA contrast. Sky Kite keeps the same soft rounded type and a fresh light page, with a blue Book button that passes.

designDirections.name: Home Care Studio
designDirections.bestFor: Established cleaning companies serving larger homes with detail cleans and standing weekly visits
designDirections.headlineSample: Careful, detailed house cleaning for {City} homes
designDirections.whyItFits: Driftwood's warm neutrals and old-style serif suit larger homes where the buyer wants discretion and care more than speed.

openers.line: Your Google listing has lovely house cleaning reviews and no Website button, so someone who wants a price for a three-bedroom clean has to call and hope you pick up.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's where that house cleaning search could land instead: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens Facebook, and the newest cleaning special there is months old. A first-time client can't tell whether that price still stands.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link. Note where it lands and the date of the newest price or special post.
openers.linkLine: A cleaning page where the price is always current: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing is a free page with a builder banner and a contact form that goes nowhere. Someone ready to book a deep clean gives up right there.
openers.hook: Open the site and find one broken thing: a dead form, an expired banner, an old number. Write it down.
openers.linkLine: The same cleaning business, with a form that books: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your cleaning site on my phone and the price table ran off the side of the screen. People shopping for a house cleaner at night are usually on the couch with a phone.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your house cleaning prices, readable on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no price anywhere for a standard clean, so a family comparing three maid services picks the one that shows a number for their bedroom and bathroom count.
openers.hook: Check the listing, posts and any site for a single published price. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A bed-and-bath price for every house cleaning visit: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your before-and-after kitchen posts from deep cleans are the best proof a cleaner can show, and they sink down the Facebook feed within a week.
openers.hook: Find one before-and-after post and note the room. Name it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: A deep clean gallery that stays put: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention your cleaners by name and say the house smelled great when they got home. Those belong right next to a Book button, not only on a map.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one phrase that names a cleaner or a room. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your cleaning reviews beside the booking page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Spring deep cleaning requests pile up fast, and the people who won't leave a voicemail book the house cleaner whose open slots they can see.
openers.hook: Use from late February to April. Check whether they posted about spring openings or a waitlist.

openers.line: The weeks before Thanksgiving are when people panic about guests and search for a one-time house cleaning. Plenty of them stay on a biweekly plan afterwards if booking was easy.
openers.hook: Use from mid-October through November. Look for a holiday post or a note about filling up.
openers.linkLine: A holiday clean that turns into a recurring one: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring house cleaners. Good applicants look you up before they apply, and a page with pay, hours and a short form gets more of them through the door.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note or a sign. Note the date and the pay if they listed it.
openers.linkLine: A cleaning company page with a hiring section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews come from {Neighborhood} and the streets around it, but nothing online says which areas your cleaning teams cover, so people a few miles out assume you won't come.
openers.hook: Find the neighbourhoods named in their reviews and pick the one furthest from their base.
openers.linkLine: A coverage page for your house cleaning routes: {demo-link}

openers.line: Leases turn over in late spring and summer, and tenants want a fixed price for an empty-apartment move-out clean plus a date. They book whoever shows both.
openers.hook: Use from May to August, or any time they post a move-out clean. Note the bedroom count.
openers.linkLine: Move-out cleaning with a fixed price and a date: {demo-link}

openers.line: Handing a house cleaner a key is a trust decision. If your team is insured and background-checked, that belongs in writing beside the Book button.
openers.hook: Look for 'insured' or 'background checked' on their listing or posts. Never claim what you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Insurance and background checks on one cleaning page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most of your cleaning clients come from neighbours tagging you in local groups. Each of them searches your name next and finds a phone number and nothing else.
openers.hook: Search their business name in local Facebook groups or Nextdoor and find one recommendation thread. Quote it.
openers.linkLine: Where a recommended house cleaner should land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is exactly the kind of clean people search for. It deserves a page where the next person can book the same clean.
openers.hook: Pick their newest cleaning post and name it: the room, the clean type, the neighbourhood if shown.
openers.linkLine: That house cleaning job on a page that books: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner} — that {specific recent job} you posted is lovely cleaning work.

I looked for a site for {Business Name} and found the Facebook page, but no way to see a price or book a clean. I put together a sample site with a bed-and-bath price list and weekly and biweekly plans, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner} — following up in case my last message got buried. Here's the sample house cleaning site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It shows a price for each bedroom and bathroom count, what a standard and a deep clean include, and a booking page with open slots. If it's not useful, say so and I'll leave you alone.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for house cleaning companies here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"No worries, you're probably mid-clean. Short version: I built a sample site for {Business Name} where people see a price for their bedroom and bathroom count and book a slot, with marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I text you the link?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"The build runs {Build Range}, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a cleaning business your size I'd normally quote about {Build Price}. One new biweekly client pays for it."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes between cleans this week?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears."

objections.objection: All my clients come from referrals.
objections.handler: "That means your cleaning is good. The referred person still looks you up before they let a stranger in with a key. The site is what they find, with your price and your re-clean promise."

objections.objection: Every house is different, I can't put prices online.
objections.handler: "You don't have to price every house. A starting price by bedroom and bathroom count, with 'final price confirmed after the first clean', stops the shoppers who only wanted a number from calling you."
"Then the site does two jobs: it fills cancellations from a waitlist, and it lets you raise prices for new clients without awkward phone calls. Full now is the best time to build it."

objections.objection: My clients just text me to reschedule.
objections.handler: "Keep that for the regulars. The site is for the new person who'd never text a number they found on a flyer. They want to see the price and press a button."

objections.objection: I already pay for a lead app.
objections.handler: "Those leads get sent to four cleaners at once. People who find your own house cleaning site only get you, and you don't pay per lead."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}, because it's the price list, the booking page and the recurring plans. One new biweekly house cleaning client covers that."

email.subject: Booking site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "Hi {Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for house cleaning companies in {City}, and I made a sample booking site for {Business Name} with your prices up front. I'll text you the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner} — I'm taking the {Business Name} cleaning demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hi {Owner} — holiday guest cleans in {City} start booking around now, and the people who book a one-time clean are the easiest to move to biweekly. Thought of you.

The booking site is still here whenever you want it, and nothing's changed on price. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a few months of one biweekly client, never to the price of a single deep clean.
The bed-and-bath price list is the core sale. Price booking, plans and add-on pages around it.
Charge more when the price list handles add-ons like inside the oven, inside the fridge and interior windows.
Price move-out and rental turnover pages one at a time; each brings a different buyer.
Keep every monthly item below the price of one recurring clean, so it never feels like losing a client.
A hiring page is often the fastest first sale in this trade. Keep it small and quick to deliver.

lineItems.description: Max with frequency discounts, a square-footage surcharge, pet and add-on pricing, and a first-clean premium shown upfront.

lineItems.item: Online booking with deposit and entry notes
lineItems.description: Max when it captures entry codes, pets and supply preferences, takes a card on file and syncs to the owner's calendar.
Max with empty-home pricing by bedroom count, a landlord checklist download and a date picker for the lease end.
Max with per-turnover pricing, linen and restocking options and a recurring turnover request for hosts.

lineItems.item: Cleaner hiring page and applicant form
lineItems.description: Max with a two-language form, availability by day, transport questions and texts to the owner for each applicant.
Max when each page names the streets served, the cleaning days for that area and reviews from clients there.
Max with gift card sales for new parents, recovery after surgery and holidays, plus a redeem-and-book flow.

whatElseYouSell.name: One-time to biweekly conversion campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Everyone who books a one-time deep clean gets a friendly note a week later offering the same cleaner every other week."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once one-time bookings come through the site.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep with weekly clean posts
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A fresh before-and-after from a real clean on your Google profile every week, so the listing looks as busy as your calendar."

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each clean
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The evening after each house cleaning visit, the client gets a short thank-you with a review link and a way to flag a missed spot first."

whatElseYouSell.name: Spring and holiday deep clean campaigns
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Two short campaigns a year, spring deep cleaning and holiday guest cleans, each pointing at open slots instead of a phone number."

whatElseYouSell.name: Car magnet and door hanger artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Door hangers for the neighbours of every house you clean, with the price-list address on them, so the street sees who just cleaned next door."

whatElseYouSell.name: Team photo morning
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One morning photographing your cleaners in uniform at a real client's kitchen, so the people you send are the faces on the site."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, at a client home that agrees in writing.

whatElseYouSell.name: Move-out cleaning mailer for leasing offices
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A one-page move-out cleaning sheet for the leasing offices near you, so tenants on their way out get your price and date picker."

whatElseYouSell.name: Spanish version of the booking pages
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The price list, the cleaning checklist and the booking page in Spanish too, for clients and for the cleaners you're hiring."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, if their team or clients speak Spanish.

withoutAI.route: The carpet cleaner they refer clients to
withoutAI.whoPays: The carpet cleaning company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When a house cleaning client asks about stained carpet, who do you send them to? That company needs a site as much as you did."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Carpet cleaners and house cleaners pass clients back and forth, and the introduction comes with a warm word.

withoutAI.route: Realtors who need move-out and listing cleans
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The agent whose listings you clean before photos needs a vendor page for sellers. Your cleaning company belongs on it, and I can build it."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents recommend vendors on every listing and pay for pages that make them look organised.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The property manager who books your move-out cleans still takes maintenance requests by voicemail. I fix that next."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers trust the cleaner who gets units rent-ready on time, and that trust gets you a meeting.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The hosts you turn over between guests need a direct-booking page for their rental. Your cleaning schedule already proves you know their calendar."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Hosts want guests booking direct, and the cleaner is the vendor they trust most.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The remodeler who calls you for dust cleanup after a kitchen job has a gallery stuck on Facebook. Introduce me."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Remodelers have bigger budgets and already rely on the cleaner to make the reveal look finished.

withoutAI.route: Professional organizers in the same homes
withoutAI.whoPays: The organizer, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The organizer who works in your house cleaning clients' closets books by phone too. Same booking layout, different service."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Organizers and cleaners share clients and refer each other, so the pitch is half done.

withAI.pitchLine: "Each new guest booking becomes a turnover clean on the cleaner's calendar, with checkout time and linen count, before the host lifts a finger."
withAI.whyItWorks: Hosts lose sleep over turnovers. The cleaning client already lives inside that problem.

withAI.pitchLine: "Sellers answer a few questions and get a room-by-room prep list, with the deep clean booked for the day before the photographer."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents want listings ready on time, and the house cleaner is the first vendor on the list.

withAI.route: Move-out instructions assistant for property managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Departing tenants ask what counts as clean, and the assistant answers from the manager's move-out checklist and offers the cleaning slot."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers field the same deposit questions every month. Cutting those calls is easy to justify.

withAI.route: Photo quote helper for the carpet cleaner
withAI.pitchLine: "Your house cleaning clients send a picture of the stain and the room size, and the carpet cleaner gets a draft quote to approve."
withAI.whyItWorks: Built for a business the cleaning client already refers to, so the introduction carries weight.

withAI.pitchLine: "Walk the finished kitchen, talk through what's left, and get a punch list with the final clean scheduled last."
withAI.whyItWorks: Remodelers hate the last week of a job. The cleaner sees that week every time.

withAI.pitchLine: "The agency whose clients you clean for turns caregiver voice notes into tidy visit notes, with a house cleaning request flagged when it's needed."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agencies share homes with the cleaner and need tidy notes. The cleaner's introduction opens the door.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back with the price list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "You're mid-clean with gloves on, the phone rings, and the caller gets a text with your bed-and-bath prices and a booking link within a minute."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs the business number forwarded and wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Day-before reminder with entry and pet notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The day before each clean, the client confirms the entry code and whether the dog is home, so your cleaner isn't stuck on the porch."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the booking calendar and a template per client type.

softwareAI.name: Skip-a-week portal for recurring clients
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Recurring clients skip a week, move a clean or add an oven clean themselves, inside your rules, instead of texting you at night."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their recurring client list, skip and cancellation rules and add-on prices.

softwareAI.name: Booking chat that quotes from the price list
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'do you clean inside the fridge' and 'what's a three-bed, two-bath' from your own house cleaning prices, then offers the next open slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the price list, checklist and booking rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Review reply and referral request drafts
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every cleaning review gets a warm reply in your voice, and happy regulars get a note asking if a neighbour needs a cleaner too."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Needs a few past replies to learn the tone. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Room-by-room checklist app with photo proof
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Cleaners tick off each room on their phone and snap the finished bathroom, so a 'you missed the shower' text gets answered with proof."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their standard and deep clean checklists and one team willing to test it.

softwareAI.name: Cleaner applicant screener in two languages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for house cleaning jobs answer your questions in English or Spanish, and you only call the ones with a car and the right days free."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any month they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves, pay and schedule. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Client home notes file
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Entry codes, pets, products to avoid and 'don't touch the piano' for every home you clean, on the cleaner's phone instead of the owner's memory."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the client list and the owner's notes, plus a rule for who sees entry codes.

softwareAI.name: After-hours booking receptionist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Someone calls at 9pm about a move-out clean, and the receptionist takes the bedroom count and lease date and books the slot."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs the calendar, prices and coverage area. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Cleaner route and day planner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Which team cleans which house on which day, grouped by neighbourhood, so nobody drives across town between two cleans."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, once they run two or more teams. Needs addresses, team list and visit lengths.

softwareAI.name: Photo estimate for deep and move-out cleans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "People send a few pictures of the oven, the bathrooms and the floors, and you get a draft deep clean price to approve before you reply."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs past deep clean prices with notes on condition. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Lapsed-client win-back
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A recurring cleaning client who hasn't booked in five weeks gets a friendly check-in with their usual day still open."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs booking history and an offer the owner is happy to make.

softwareAI.name: Tip and pay tracker per cleaner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each cleaner sees their hours, their cleans and the tips clients left, so payday questions stop landing on the owner."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs pay rules and how tips are collected today.

softwareAI.name: Client message sorter
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Reschedules, add-on requests and 'the cleaner missed the stairs' messages get sorted and drafted, so the owner answers ten texts in two minutes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs the shared business inbox or text line. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Job costing per house
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which recurring houses take longer than the price allows, so the owner raises the right cleaning prices instead of all of them."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a few months of visit times from the checklist app and current prices.

softwareAI.name: Cleaner training assistant from the owner's checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New cleaners ask the phone how the owner wants a glass shower or a marble counter done, and get the owner's answer in their language."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the written cleaning standards and the owner's approval of every answer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Gift card and referral credit ledger
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Gift cleans and refer-a-neighbour credits tracked in one place, applied automatically at the next booking."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their gift card rules and referral offer.

softwareAI.name: Open-slot filler for the waitlist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a recurring client cancels Thursday's clean, the waitlist nearest that street gets a text offering the slot, written in your voice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, once a waitlist exists. Needs the calendar and waitlist. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Supply and laundry tracker per team
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each cleaning team marks low spray bottles, cloths and vacuum bags, and the owner sees one shopping list on Friday."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the team kit list and who restocks.

softwareAI.name: Post-clean survey and re-clean request
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Two hours after each clean the client rates the visit, and a low score books a free re-clean instead of a bad review."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs the re-clean promise wording and the booking calendar.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the skip-a-week portal for house cleaning companies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built a recurring-client portal for one house cleaning company. Every maid service has clients texting to skip a week."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The first client paid for the build and taught you the skip and cancellation rules every cleaning business has.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: License the bed-and-bath price list to a cleaning supply distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Give every house cleaner who buys from you a price list and booking page, with your supply reorder built in."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors want small cleaning companies loyal, and a tool they use daily beats a coupon.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member maid service a booking site template with a re-clean promise page as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need renewal reasons, and one agreement reaches many owners at once.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each of your house cleaning territories needs its own price list, neighbourhood pages and a booking calendar that routes to the right owner."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract, many territories, one template built from a real independent's site.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: White-label cleaning site template for agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency keeps getting house cleaning clients and building from scratch. License my booking template with the bed-and-bath pricing done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the client relationship; you sell them the part you've already got right.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Move-out cleaning vendor board for property management firms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every unit that turns over gets a move-out clean booked from one board, across all the cleaning vendors you use."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Large firms chase turnover cleans every month, and the cleaning client's workflow proves you understand it.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Turnover board for short-term rental co-host networks
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every property you co-host, every cleaner, every checkout, on one turnover board that the house cleaners actually like using."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Co-hosts manage many cleaners across many rentals and pay to stop the group-text chaos.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: The same house cleaning stack in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: New cleaning clients in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one house cleaning company per area, and {City} is taken. Your side of the metro is still open."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Non-competing geography lets you reuse the price list, the booking flow and the proof.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The coach or course, per student or flat fee
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your students all need a house cleaning site with prices and booking. Bundle my template into the course."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Coaches sell to new cleaning owners who all need the same site, and the coach brings the buyers.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Move-in cleaning for corporate relocation firms
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every employee you move into a rental needs a move-in clean. One booking page with vetted cleaners in each city."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Relocation firms buy convenience for employees and pay for vendor pages that save their coordinators calls.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Resident cleaning booking for senior living communities
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Residents and their families book an apartment clean from one page, and your house cleaning partner gets the schedule."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Communities want to offer more services without hiring, and a trusted cleaner makes the offer real.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Someone started a booking or skip-a-week tool for your cleaning business and vanished. I've shipped that exact flow before."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Stranded owners already decided to buy. They want someone who has finished one.

upsellLadder.offer: House cleaning booking site plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The cleaning site and the care plan go on one contract, so a new price or a holiday closure is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: A month live, and at least one new client has booked through the site.
upsellLadder.line: "That first online booking was a stranger. The next one comes faster when the reviews show up after every clean."

upsellLadder.trigger: Booking data shows several one-time deep cleans that never came back.
upsellLadder.line: "Those deep clean clients already let you in. A note offering the same cleaner every other week brings a few of them back."

upsellLadder.trigger: They complain about evening texts from clients moving their cleans.
upsellLadder.line: "Those texts about skipping a week can go to a page that follows your cleaning rules."

upsellLadder.offer: Cleaner applicant screener in two languages
upsellLadder.trigger: They post a hiring note or turn down new clients for lack of cleaners.
upsellLadder.line: "You're turning away house cleaning work for lack of hands. Let's fill the applicant list first."

upsellLadder.trigger: The missed-call log shows evening calls about move-out or deep cleans going unanswered.
upsellLadder.line: "Those evening calls are move-out cleans on a deadline. The receptionist books them while you're off."

upsellLadder.trigger: They add a second or third cleaning team.
upsellLadder.line: "Two teams crossing town between cleans costs you an hour a day. Group the houses by neighbourhood."
